newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty firms above 3.5 pct from parity, depos flat.
newsitem.headline: Zloty firms above 3.5 pct from parity, depos flat.

text.p: The zloty firmed against the trading band centre breaking resistance at 3.50 percent from the parity rate amid currency selling likely spurred by foreign investor entry into Polish stocks, dealers said.
They said the central bank was only checking levels on the local forex market but did not intervene against the zloty.
They said the zloty was also helped by the dollar's easing against the mark on world markets.
"The currency selling trend likely came from foreign investors entering the Polish stock market," said Leszek Szafranek from Bank Slaski SA.

The zloty closed at 3.58/3.50 percent from the trading band centre, stronger than Monday's close at 3.38/3.33 percent. It closed at 3.0360/80 to the dollar, down from 3.0350/60 on Monday and at 1.7845/65 to the mark, up from 1.7912/20.
Dealers said foreign entry into the Polish bourse was not large but enough to push the upward zloty on the shallow Polish market.
"Several million dollars daily (of foreign entry into the Polish bourse) is enough to lift zloty rate higher," said a dealer at a foreign bank here.
One-day rates were flat despite an NBP drainage of 296 million zlotys and a 238 million zloty NBP-bill sale.
The NBP raised the maximum 14-day reverse repo rate by 0.01 point to 21.65 percent and average NBP-bill yields were flat at 21.99 percent for 91 days and 22.00 percent for 182 days.
Comparable 13-week and 26-week T-bills were sold at average yields of 19.77 percent and 19.95 percent at Monday tender.
Overnight rates were quoted at 21.25/21.59 percent against opening's 21.37/21.55 percent and tomorrow/next rates were at 21.25/21.65 percent against 21.35/21.60 percent.
